$comment: Stage 6 control bands — see AI_NATIVE_SDLC.md and .sdlc/intents/sdlc-locks-evals-bands/. A band is a metric with a stable baseline, watched by scripts/control-bands.ts. Detection is deterministic; no model decides a breach. Add a band only for a metric whose baseline is genuinely stable. Bands with the `benchmark-json` collector are produced by `npm run bench` (benchmarks/bands.ts is the registry, and benchmarks/bands.test.ts fails when the two files disagree) — a band here that nothing emits reports "band not computed yet" forever, which reads exactly like a healthy young band. Compat bands are NOT listed here: scripts/control-bands.ts derives one per file in packages/compat-oracle/baseline/, so a package lane adds a band by adding its baseline fragment and never touches this file.

bands.description: Wall-clock of `npm test` (root locks + package suites), in ms
Rules on at error in eslint.config.mjs (every Interlace rule, minus documented exceptions)
Interlace rules switched off here as documented false positives; should only shrink

B1 — median tokens an agent spends per benchmark task on the floor-meeting demo (`npm run bench -- --axis agent`). Needs CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; without one the axis reports skipped and this band is fed nothing, deliberately.
B1 — median turns (`num_turns`) an agent spends per benchmark task on the floor-meeting demo. Skipped without a credential, exactly as the tokens band is.

B2 — cold start of `burgee/commander` over cold start of commander itself, median of paired spawns interleaved in one run. A ratio rather than a duration: absolute ms is a property of the runner, and a band over it would be a band over which machine picked up the job.

B4 — bytes a user's bundle grows by for `import 'burgee'`, esbuild-minified over a one-import fixture. Bytes rather than KB: a 400-byte regression is invisible once rounded, and this ratchet exists to catch exactly the accidental kind of growth.
B4 — the same measurement for `burgee/commander`, the front-end that replaces commander.
B4 — the same measurement for `burgee/yargs`, the front-end that replaces yargs.
Share of tasks where our demo's exit code told an agent the right class of thing: 0 ok, 2 rewrite the command, any other non-zero retryable (benchmarks axis `reliability`)
Share of `--json` tasks where our demo emitted an addressable envelope on the stream that carried it (benchmarks axis `reliability`)
Non-TTY runs per 100 where our demo waited for a human instead of exiting. A hang is a failed agent task every time (benchmarks axis `reliability`)

agent-headroom R7 — bytes of `--schema` on the burgee demo, the whole document an agent reads to discover the CLI. Compact by default since R1 (39,512 -> 22,964 B on the large demo, byte-identical parse); this band is what keeps a well-meaning "make the output readable" commit from giving the 42% back, because no test fails when it does.
